name: Market entry
summary: Should we enter, and if so how? Assess market attractiveness, competition, the client's ability to win, the economics, and the entry mode, then weigh the risks.
opening_line: To decide whether to enter I'd look at four things: how attractive the market is, how competitive it is, whether we have what it takes to win, and whether the economics work. Then I'd look at the best way in.
when_to_use: Entering a new geography, customer segment or product category
Launching into a market the client hasn't served
when_not_to_use: The client is already in the market and profits are falling: use profitability
The main question is which company to buy: use M&A (though entry mode may include acquisition)

children.label: Right to win: brand, tech, cost

buckets.name: Market attractiveness
questions: How big is the market, and how fast is it growing?

buckets.name: Competition
questions: Who are the leaders, and how concentrated is it?
Is there a gap we can exploit?

buckets.name: Client capabilities
questions: Can we leverage existing assets (brand, channels, plants)?
What would we need to build or acquire?

buckets.name: Economics
questions: What share can we realistically win, and by when?
What's the upfront investment and breakeven?
Does it meet the client's return hurdle?

buckets.name: Entry mode & risks
questions: Build, buy or partner? Speed vs control vs cost
What could go wrong: execution, cannibalisation, regulatory?

industry_adaptations.note: Attractiveness = patient population × diagnosis/treatment rates × price (reimbursement). Barriers: regulatory approval timeline, patents, payer access.
Entry economics per store: sales per sq ft, build-out capex, rent. Consider local competition, real estate and supply chain reach.
Look at TAM by segment, switching costs and network effects of incumbents, and CAC/payback in the new segment.
Unit economics per location (AUV, four-wall margin), site selection, franchise vs company-owned.
For governments or non-profits entering a programme area, replace 'profit' with impact per dollar and stakeholder support.

common_mistakes: Skipping 'client capabilities': an attractive market isn't enough if the client can't win
No numbers: failing to size the prize or compute breakeven
